decision: A complete capability-preserving backport is not established as bounded. Retain the source and inert regression/build inputs; do not create a partial provider patch or register an override.

scope.nativeBrowserBoundary: The exact Chrome 155.0.8059.84 source exposes viewportMeta enable/default and media feature overrides. That source observation supports keeping the native revision; actual browser behavior remains untested.
scope.boundary: File differences include annotations, formatting and generated schema changes as well as behavior. This count is not a claim that all 63 modules need backporting. Seven additional stable published modules have no corresponding alpha module map; absence is not treated as an intentional removal.

commandDelta.referenceBehavior: Implemented. Validates the supported Blink feature names before changing configuration, supports global/user/browsing-context settings, propagates the effective setting to related frame targets, and sends Emulation.setEmulatedMedia. Null removes the override.

Implemented. Accepts true or null, supports scoped configuration and inheritance, and shares the metrics path with viewport, pixel ratio, orientation, screen area and scrollbar settings. The viewport-meta-only case must not clear device metrics. Target initialization must apply inherited settings to new targets.
Parsed and rejected with unsupported operation. Stable has no corresponding case. Do not invent a successful implementation or count this as a working feature.

additionalBehaviorDifferences.evidence: Reference stores per-top-level-context cache behavior, applies it to children and newly configured targets, and clears scoped settings on a global change. Stable stores only a global default and applies context changes to the currently selected target.
additionalBehaviorDifferences.implication: A two-command backport alone cannot establish preservation of current cache behavior across child target creation or replacement.

additionalBehaviorDifferences.evidence: Reference fetches current bounds and restores a non-normal window before resizing or transitioning. Stable directly sends the final bounds. Reference also maps missing-window errors differently.
additionalBehaviorDifferences.implication: Preservation needs a protocol-faithful regression and actual headful browser proof beyond the two emulation methods.

additionalBehaviorDifferences.evidence: Reference passes targetInfo.type into CdpTarget; distinguishes page, frame and worker domains; and forwards browser/custom-session CDP events. Stable lacks that target-type constructor input and those event-forwarding paths.
additionalBehaviorDifferences.implication: Copying the two target methods without tracing target initialization omits required guards or imports unrelated target behavior. Worker/CDP capabilities require explicit preservation evidence.

additionalBehaviorDifferences.evidence: Reference scopes preload channels by target and sandbox, resets/waits for the active default realm differently, and handles initial popup navigation, BFCache restore and download navigation attribution differently.
additionalBehaviorDifferences.implication: Realm, evaluateOnNewDocument, popup, frame replacement and navigation acceptance cannot be inferred from matching command names.

additionalBehaviorDifferences.evidence: Reference adds goog:hasCrossSiteAncestor validation/filtering and goog:partitionKey conversion. Stable lacks these paths.
additionalBehaviorDifferences.boundary: Puppeteer 25.15.0's inspected BiDi converter still rejects hasCrossSiteAncestor:true. This is a provider capability difference, not a claim that Puppeteer's current public BiDi API accepts that input.

missingInputs.required: Retained, license-identified CDDL/spec source at an exact revision with bounded additions for the required commands and public Command/Emulation unions.
missingInputs.observed: The complete stable repository archive has generated protocol TypeScript and Zod sources, but no .cddl file. Its tools/generate-bidi-types.mjs requires an external --cddl-file. Generated headers cite mutable W3C master, not an exact input revision.

missingInputs.required: An owner-selected pinned protocol generator and schema-family path, or a reviewed source-owned extension design that generates all required public types and parsers without hand-editing generated files.
missingInputs.observed: Stable uses cddlconv 0.1.7 and Zod ^3.24.1. Reference uses cddlconv 0.2.0 and Zod ^4.6.5; parseObject changes error.errors to error.issues, and generated enum/value exports change. Neither cddlconv nor a provider schema-family selection is in the owning Puck catalog.

missingInputs.required: Owning catalog entries and reviewed dependency delivery for the provider runtime/protocol/schema dependencies, bundler and third-party license handling.
missingInputs.observed: Puck currently catalogs Node, TS7, pnpm and esbuild. It does not catalog chromium-bidi, devtools-protocol, mitt, zod, cddlconv, rollup, @rollup/plugin-node-resolve, rollup-plugin-cleanup or rollup-plugin-license. Upstream GN/Ninja and external DEPS/CIPD inputs are retained references, not installed/reviewed Puck execution inputs.

missingInputs.required: Trace the additional behavior changes affecting current capabilities, define the exact source correction set, and prove preservation rather than assuming two missing dispatcher cases exhaust the compatibility work.
missingInputs.observed: Source inspection identifies the additional differences above; no complete preservation proof or accepted reduction in capability exists.

missingInputs.required: Parent-controlled execution after the primary lease is available and frozen catalog/install-age issues are resolved.
missingInputs.observed: Human explicitly prohibits tests, builds, installs, typechecks, generation and browser execution during this sidecar. No result is claimed for the inert inputs.

nonClaims: No provider source correction, compiled patch, override, dependency declaration or patch registration has been implemented.
No alpha module, declaration or IIFE has been relabeled or copied into a stable candidate.
Source/CDP-schema support is not actual browser behavior or compatibility acceptance.
No production, release, owner-approval or readiness claim.
